text: In a rectangular park measuring 50 m × 40 m, a company plans to construct a rectangular swimming pool in the middle, surrounded by a uniform-width grass strip throughout the park. Find the dimensions of the swimming pool if the area of the grassy strip is 1184 m².

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Quadratic Equations; formation and solution from an area condition
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q32
meta.extractiveQuote: In a rectangular park measuring 50 m × 40 m, a company plans to construct a rectangular swimming pool in the middle, surrounded by a uniform-width grass strip throughout the park. Find the dimensions of the swimming pool if the area of the grassy strip is 1184 m².

text: Let x m be the uniform width of the grass strip. Then the pool dimensions are (50 − 2x) m by (40 − 2x) m. The area of the park minus the pool area is 1184 m²: 50×40 − (50 − 2x)(40 − 2x) = 1184, giving x² − 45x + 296 = 0 = (x − 8)(x − 37). Reject x = 37 because it makes the pool dimensions negative; x = 8. Therefore the pool is 50 − 16 = 34 m long and 40 − 16 = 24 m wide.

text: Carbon forms millions of compounds whereas silicon, which is just below it in the Periodic Table, forms a few compounds. Explain the reason for the difference in their ability to form compounds.

meta.subject: science
conceptTags: Carbon and its compounds; catenation; atomic size and bond strength
meta.heading: Science (086) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q25
meta.extractiveQuote: Carbon forms millions of compounds whereas silicon, which is just below it in the Periodic Table, forms a few compounds. Explain the reason for the difference in their ability to form compounds.

text: Carbon forms millions of compounds because its small atomic size allows it to form strong, stable C–C bonds and show extensive catenation. Silicon has a larger atomic size and forms weaker Si–Si bonds, so it cannot show catenation to the same extent and forms fewer compounds.

text: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Circles; equal tangents from an external point
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q29
meta.extractiveQuote: Prove that a parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.

text: Let the circle touch sides AB, BC, CD and DA at S, P, Q and R, respectively. Tangents from the same external point are equal: AS = AR, BS = BP, CQ = CP and DQ = DR. Adding gives AB + CD = AD + BC. In a parallelogram, AB = CD and AD = BC, so 2AB = 2AD and AB = AD. Adjacent sides are equal; therefore the parallelogram is a rhombus.

text: If 1/(sin x − cos x) = cosec x/√2, then prove that (1/(sin x + cos x))² = sec² x/2.

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Introduction to Trigonometry; trigonometric identity proof
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q31(B)
meta.extractiveQuote: If 1/(sin x − cos x) = cosec x/√2, then prove that (1/(sin x + cos x))² = sec² x/2.

text: Given 1/(sin x − cos x) = cosec x/√2, so sin x − cos x = √2 sin x. Squaring gives 2 sin x cos x = 1 − 2 sin²x. Then (1/(sin x + cos x))² = 1/(1 + 2 sin x cos x) = 1/[1 + (1 − 2 sin²x)] = 1/(2 cos²x) = sec²x/2, as required.

text:
Basic Proportionality Theorem: In triangle ABC, let D lie on AB and E lie on AC with DE ∥ BC. The triangles BDE and CDE have equal areas because they share base DE and lie between the same parallels DE and BC. Also, area(△ADE)/area(△BDE) = AD/DB, using their altitudes to AB; and area(△ADE)/area(△CDE) = AE/EC, using their altitudes to AC. Since area(△BDE) = area(△CDE), AD/DB = AE/EC.
For the trapezium, draw diagonal PR meeting XY at M. In △PSR, XM ∥ SR, so PX/XS = PM/MR. In △PQR, MY ∥ PQ, so QY/YR = PM/MR. Therefore PX/XS = QY/YR.

text: A tent is in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a conical top. The height and radius of the cylindrical part are 3 m and 14 m, respectively, and the total height of the tent is 13.5 m. Find the canvas area required, allowing 26 m² for stitching and wastage. Also find the cost of the canvas at ₹250 per m².

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Surface Areas and Volumes; cone and cylinder curved surface area
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q34(A)
meta.extractiveQuote: A tent is in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a conical top. The height and radius of the cylindrical part are 3 m and 14 m, respectively, and the total height of the tent is 13.5 m. Find the canvas area required, allowing 26 m² for stitching and wastage. Also find the cost of the canvas at ₹250 per m².

text: The cone height is 13.5 − 3 = 10.5 m and its slant height is √(14² + 10.5²) = 17.5 m. Cone curved surface area = πrl = 770 m²; cylinder curved surface area = 2πrh = 264 m². Including 26 m² for stitching and wastage, the canvas area is 770 + 264 + 26 = 1060 m². Cost = 1060 × ₹250 = ₹265,000.

text: A solid wooden toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone of the same radius. The radius of the hemisphere is 3.5 cm and the total volume of wood used is 166 5/6 cm³. Find the height of the conical part. Also find the cost of painting the hemispherical part at ₹15 per cm².

meta.subject: maths
conceptTags: Surface Areas and Volumes; cone and hemisphere volume and curved surface area
meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q34(B)
meta.extractiveQuote: A solid wooden toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone of the same radius. The radius of the hemisphere is 3.5 cm and the total volume of wood used is 166 5/6 cm³. Find the height of the conical part. Also find the cost of painting the hemispherical part at ₹15 per cm².

text: Let h cm be the cone height. The total volume is (1/3)π(3.5)²h + (2/3)π(3.5)³ = 166 5/6 cm³, giving h = 6 cm. The curved surface area of the hemisphere is 2π(3.5)² = 77 cm². Painting cost = 77 × ₹15 = ₹1,155.

meta.heading: Mathematics Standard (041) Sample Question Paper 2026-27 · Q35(A)
meta.extractiveQuote: Manish is standing on level ground and observes a kite flying 200 m away from him at an angle of elevation of 30°.
